ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Global Sensitivity Analysis for High-Dimensional Models using the Shapley Value Decomposition
PROPOSAL: Perform an empirical study on the scalability and performance of the SHAP library, specifically the KernelSHAP estimator, on a variety of high-dimensional datasets from different domains (e.g. image classification, natural language processing, recommender systems) and models (e.g. neural networks, gradient boosting machines) to explore its feasibility and limitations for large-scale Shapley value computation. Compare the results to a baseline of exact Shapley value calculation for small subsets of features.
CONTROLS: Compare against exact Shapley value calculation for small subsets, use random Shapley value estimation as a baseline for unfeasible exact calculation.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The study should reveal the challenges of high-dimensional Shapley value computation but also show the effectiveness of the KernelSHAP estimator on smaller datasets, with a possible failure in capturing the full complexity of the underlying model for very high-dimensional inputs.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Non-Asymptotic Sample Complexity Analysis of KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Provide a theoretical analysis of the sample complexity of KernelSHAP, proving non-asymptotic bounds on the error between the estimated Shapley values and the true Shapley values. Assume a Gaussian distribution for the kernel weights and leverage the techniques of deviation inequalities and compression to derive a high-probability bound on the difference between the empirical Shapley values and the population Shapley values.
CONTROLS: Comparison with known bounds for LeverageSHAP, consideration of the impact of regularization on the convergence rate.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: The analysis should reveal a tradeoff between sample size and the desired precision, with a possible failure in deriving sharp bounds for very large dimensions or complex feature dependencies.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: A Comparison of KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and Unbiased KernelSHAP on Real-World Datasets
PROPOSAL: Conduct an experimental study to compare the performance and scalability of the three estimators (KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and Unbiased KernelSHAP) on a range of real-world datasets and models, evaluating their ability to accurately recover the true Shapley values and their computational efficiency. Use metrics such as mean absolute error (MAE), R-squared, and computation time to compare the results.
CONTROLS: Exact Shapley value calculation as a baseline for small subsets of features, random Shapley value estimation for unfeasible exact calculation.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: LeverageSHAP is likely to outperform KernelSHAP and Unbiased KernelSHAP across most datasets and scenarios, while Unbiased KernelSHAP might underperform due to its unbiased nature, with a possible failure in capturing the niche scenarios where one of the methods excels.

ACTION: REVISE 
TITLE: Non-Asymptotic Sample Complexity Analysis of KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Strengthen the previous proposal by deriving tighter bounds on the sample complexity of KernelSHAP by assuming an alpha-mixing process for the feature dependencies and leveraging techniques from rate-distortion theory. This should provide a better understanding of the relationships between the number of samples, feature dimensionality, and desired precision.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing bounds for LeverageSHAP, sensitivity analysis to alpha-mixing process parameters.
COST: 258.19
PREDICTION: Tighter bounds should be achievable, but the analysis may become more complex and break down for very large dimensions or complex feature dependencies due to the strict assumptions on the feature distribution and correlation structure.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Non-Asymptotic Sample Complexity Analysis of KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Strengthen the previous proposal by deriving tighter bounds on the sample complexity of KernelSHAP by assuming an alpha-mixing process for the feature dependencies and leveraging techniques from rate-distortion theory. This should provide a better understanding of the relationships between the number of samples, feature dimensionality, and desired precision.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing bounds for LeverageSHAP, sensitivity analysis to alpha-mixing process parameters, assuming realistic feature distributions (e.g. uniform, Gaussian, correlated).
COST: 198
PREDICTION: Tighter bounds should be achievable, but the analysis may become more complex and break down for very large dimensions or complex feature dependencies due to the strict assumptions on the feature distribution and correlation structure.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Approximate Shapley Sampling Schemes for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Investigate and compare different sampling schemes for KernelSHAP, focusing on trade-offs between computational efficiency, statistical accuracy, and threat to model interpretability. This includes variant sampling distributions (e.g. sampling with or without replacement), as well as pairings of samples for accounting for correlations. Evaluate these methods on a range of datasets and compare to the standard KernelSHAP variant.
CONTROLS: Comparison to standard KernelSHAP, consideration of the impact of different sampling schemes on estimation accuracy, computational efficiency, and interpretability.
COST: 270
PREDICTION: Some sampling schemes should substantially improve efficiency without significant loss in accuracy or interpretability, but others might have uncorrectable biases or challenges for certain data characteristics.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: A Theoretical Framework for Shapley Value Estimation via Regularized Empirical Risk Minimization
PROPOSAL: Provide a unified framework for understanding and analyzing the performance of various Shapley value estimators, including KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and others, through the lens of empirical risk minimization (ERM) and regularization theory. Derive bounds on the estimation error in terms of the regularization strength and the complexity of the underlying model.
CONTROLS: Evaluation on simulated and real-world datasets, comparison with existing bounds for specific estimators.
COST: 333.220
PREDICTION: The framework should provide insights into the value of regularization for balancing bias-variance trade-offs in Shapley value estimation, with a possible failure to capture the intricacies of high-dimensional or modal-rich data scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Scalable Shapley Values via Adaptive Model Approximations
PROPOSAL: Develop a method to adaptively approximate the underlying model in the Shapley value computation, allowing for efficient computation even for complex high-dimensional models. This is accomplished by iteratively refining a surrogate model, using the Shapley value estimation as a guide to determine the quality of the approximation. Evaluate the method on a range of datasets and models, comparing to exact Shapley value computation and other approximation methods.
CONTROLS: Comparison to exact Shapley value computation, evaluation on a range of datasets and models.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: The adaptive approximation method should significantly improve computational efficiency for high-dimensional models, potentially at the cost of estimation accuracy or interpretability in some scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Using Domain Knowledge to Improve Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the potential benefits of incorporating domain-specific knowledge into Shapley value estimation, such as incorporating prior knowledge about feature relationships or incorporating domain-specific objectives into the estimation process. This could include approaches such as using prior distributions to regularize the Shapley values or incorporating domain-specific constraints into the estimation procedure. Evaluate the methods on a range of datasets and models.
CONTROLS: Comparison to standard Shapley value estimation, evaluation on a range of datasets and models.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Incorporating domain knowledge should lead to improved Shapley value estimation in many scenarios, but may also introduce new challenges or sources of bias that must be carefully managed.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Benchmarking Shapley Value Estimators on a Comprehensive Suite of Datasets and Models
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive benchmarking suite for Shapley value estimators, including a wide range of datasets, models, and evaluation metrics. Use this benchmarking suite to thoroughly evaluate the performance of various Shapley value estimators, including the ones proposed in this set of experiments, and to identify areas for future research and improvement.
CONTROLS: Evaluation on a comprehensive range of datasets, models, and evaluation metrics; comparison to state-of-the-art baselines.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The benchmarking suite should provide a fundamental resource for the Shapley value community, helping to identify which methods are most effective in different scenarios and revealing new challenges and areas for future research.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Multimodal Sampling for Temporal Evolution Description
PROPOSAL: We adapt non-autoregressive image-to-text transformers, specifically the sixty-four variant of Vision Transformer (ViT) and the VL backbone, to learn multimodal representations from sequences of satellite images, using a query-based sampling mechanism to focus on informative patches and selectively attend to temporally relevant image regions.
CONTROLS: Comparison to existing temporal change description methods (e.g., temporal residual networks, recurrent neural network-based approaches), along with a strong baseline using a video-capable Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) with static image captioning on each frame.
COST: 94500
PREDICTION: Expected to outperform existing methods on change description by a moderate margin; potential failure: difficulty in reconciling the need for enough temporal context to understand evolution with the limited capacity of non-autoregressive models under stringent pacing, leading to an overemphasis on early events.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Temporal Evolution and Forecasting with Augmented Continual Learning
PROPOSAL: We introduce an augmented continual learning framework that leverages pre-trained models, thereafter gradually incorporating new data-points in a sparse and temporally ordered manner, while addressing catastrophic forgetting through loss-based and knowledge-based regularization.
CONTROLS: Evolution description experiment using pre-trained models without transfer learning as an ablation, forecasting experiment with random initialization as a baseline.
COST: 115892.5
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in both tasks due to utilizing pre-trained models; transfer learning could further outperform baseline experiments in forecasting but may exhibit vulnerability to catastrophic forgetting, particularly on images depicting significant changes or structural damage, though additional regularization should mitigate such risks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing Temporal Forecasting Error through Causal Attribution
PROPOSAL: We use a proxy-based causal attribution approach centered around the concept of Shapley values to provide insights into why forecasts from existing models deviate from the true future state, allowing us to probe into model limitations and highlight potential avenues for improvement.
CONTROLS: Experiment with temporal forecasting using the same augmented continual learning framework as in proposal 2, with causal attribution analysis for identifying potential model biases; comparison to random expectations as a lower bound for understanding model error.
COST: 16920
PREDICTION: This attribution-based analysis will reveal that current limitations in forecasting primarily stem from difficulties in accurately modeling long-term low-probability events (e.g., unanticipated natural disasters) and rare transitions between state clusters, rather than issues with overall trend accuracy or basic structural changes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Customized Loss Functions for Temporal Consistency in Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose two novel loss functions to directly evaluate temporal consistency in satellite image forecasting: (a) the Temporal Insulation Loss, which encourages generated images to diverge as little as possible from their historical counterparts, and (b) the Causal Flow Entropy Loss, which favors forecasts that maintain the entropic structure of past causal flows.
CONTROLS: Experiments with both loss functions, when used separately and in combination, alongside a baseline using standard mean squared error (MSE) to evaluate forecasting quality; ablation study using just temporal insulation loss to demonstrate its potential improvement on simple task of matching precise change timing.
COST: 27720
PREDICTION: Both proposed loss functions should significantly improve the temporal consistency of forecasts generated by current models; when combined, they may lead to marginal gains in direct image forecasting metrics like MSE, although this might come at the cost of model complexity and increased computational demands.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Temporal Evolution and Forecasting with Augmented Continual Learning
PROPOSAL: We modify our previous approach to include explicitly modeling the interaction between the pre-trained model and the continually learned tasks, utilizing a separate transformer for each time step to adapt to the changing landscape while preserving the learned knowledge, and adding a temporal coherence regularization to prevent catastrophic forgetting.
CONTROLS: Transfer learning experiment with static model as an ablation, forecasting experiment without the coherence regularization, in addition to the standard continual learning baseline.
COST: 150000
PREDICTION: Revamped approach is expected to close the gap in forecasting quality between transfer learning and random initialization and potentially yield improvements in change description accuracy, but its improved performance might be at the cost of overall forecasting efficiency, and reduced ability to generalize across domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Combining Change Description and Forecasting using Causal Graph Reasoning
PROPOSAL: We leverage pre-trained models' change description capabilities and apply causality-based link prediction to dynamically construct temporal causal graphs from historical image sequences, incorporating which into a neural generative model to direct the forecasting process and inject causal reasoning.
CONTROLS: Change description and forecasting experiments with causal graph inputs, in addition to an ablation without causal graph inputs; comparison to transfer learning and random initialization forecasting baselines, as well as standard graph-based approaches.
COST: 35250
PREDICTION: This reasoning-based approach is likely to enhance forecasting performance and temporal consistency by emphasizing causative drivers behind change, possibly by even closing the gap with scenarios of perfect structural knowledge, but its efficacy may decrease when faced with complex, unforeseen changes due to limitations in model interpretability and the potential overfitting to the established causal graph.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporally Consistent Satellite Image Forecasting through Latent Space Transformations
PROPOSAL: We propose utilizing a Gaussian process transformation to model the temporal evolution of learned latent space representations, thereby capturing long-term patterns and creating temporally consistent forecasts by injecting the dynamic temporal structure into the generation process.
CONTROLS: Forecasts generated using GP-transformed latent spaces and compared against baseline experiments without GP transformations, transfer learning, and the proposed causal graph-based approach; ablation study to evaluate the necessity of GP-based temporal coherence modeling.
COST: 43325
PREDICTION: The incorporation of GP-based temporal coherence modeling is expected to lead to a significant improvement in temporal consistency, and likely positive effects on overall forecasting quality, due to its ability to better handle long-term dynamics; however, there is potential for decreased overall performance if not enough training data is available to accurately capture the underlying temporal patterns.

ACTION: REVISE 6
TITLE: Temporally Consistent Satellite Image Forecasting through Latent Space Transformations
PROPOSAL: We modify our previous approach by injecting a temporal denoising autoencoder (TDAE) to regularize the GP transformations and better capture the underlying temporal dynamics, thereby enhancing the overall forecasting performance and consistency.
CONTROLS: Experiment comparing GP-transformed latent spaces with and without TDAE regularization; ablation study with just GP transformations to isolate the benefits of TD specialist on T-conditioned forecasting; forecasting experiments against transfer learning, causal graph-based approach, and GP-free baselines.
COST: 166537.5
PREDICTION: By incorporating TDAE regularization, our proposed approach is predicted to outperform the original GP-based method in terms of forecasting quality, but may be limited by the potential trade-off between denoising performance and TD modelling accuracy, particularly in scenarios with heavy tailed distributions or correlated error sources.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation and Refining of Satellite Image Forecasts through Adversarial Training
PROPOSAL: We propose incorporating human feedback through an iterative evaluation process to refine generated satellite image forecasts, utilizing this feedback to update the forecasting model via an adversarial training mechanism that refines the model's ability to adapt to subtle changes and unusual patterns not apparent in training data.
CONTROLS: Iterative evaluation and refinement process with and without adversarial training; ablation study to isolate the benefits of human feedback in improving forecasting quality; comparison to baselines using traditional forecast evaluation metrics and transfer learning approaches.
COST: 56250
PREDICTION: Human-in-the-loop evaluation and refinement process, when combined with adversarial training, should significantly improve the overall forecasting performance, particularly in capturing subtle changes, but potential risks of introducing biased feedback from non-experts and complexities in interhuman variability in labeling may compromise model quality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficiency-Consistency Tradeoff Analysis in Satellite Image Forecasting via Model Compression and Ensemble Methods
PROPOSAL: We investigate various model compression and ensemble techniques to identify tradeoff points between forecasting efficiency (i.e., computational resources required) and consistency in satellite image forecasting, thereby optimizing the use of computational resources and identifying suitable models for real-world application scenarios.
CONTROLS: Experiment with multiple model compression techniques (e.g., knowledge distillation, pruning, quantization) and ensemble methods (e.g., bagging, boosting, stacking); ablation study to isolate the impact of individual compression and ensemble techniques on model performance; comparison to baselines with unchanged model complexity.
COST: 72900
PREDICTION: By identifying optimal model compression and ensemble strategies, we expect to achieve a desirable tradeoff between forecasting efficiency and consistency, enabling efficient use of computational resources for real-world applications, but potential risks of overfitting to specific scenarios or datasets might require additional regularizations.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating the Efficacy of Frozen Base Models with Adaptive Layers for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of a set of pre-trained deep forecasting models (e.g., Prophet, LSTM, and GRU) with frozen base models and adaptive layers (e.g., simple multilayer perceptrons) against a set of models with unfrozen base models and no adaptive layers on a range of real-world benchmarks (e.g., traffic flow prediction on the PeMS dataset and electricity consumption on the M4 competition dataset).
CONTROLS: Compare against baseline models with unfrozen base models and no adaptive layers (e.g., vanilla Prophet, LSTM, and GRU).
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: We expect the frozen base models with adaptive layers to outperform the unfrozen base models, particularly on the longer-term forecasts, due to the reduced destabilization from single-sample updates and adaptability to changing conditions, but may struggle when adapting to sudden concept drifts without sufficient updating authority.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Comparison of Ensembling Strategies for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of various ensembling strategies (e.g., bagging, boosting, and stacking) applied to a set of online learned models (e.g., incremental ARIMA, online LSTM, and incremental GRU) on multiple real-world benchmarks (e.g., traffic flow prediction on the PeMS dataset, electricity consumption on the M4 competition dataset, and exchange rate forecasting on the FX data).
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline model using a single, pre-trained deep model (e.g., Prophet or a static LSTM) on the same benchmarks.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: We expect ensembling strategies to significantly improve the accuracy of online forecasts, particularly when combining incremental models, but ensembling methods may require a large number of base models and may not adapt well to concept drifts without fine-tuning.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Evaluating the Utilization of Historical Data through Experience Replay for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Implement experience replay strategies (e.g., sampling from a buffer of historical data, injecting synthetic episodes, or progressive sampling) to supplement online learning for a set of pre-trained deep forecasting models (e.g., Prophet, LSTM, and GRU) on real-world benchmarks (e.g., traffic flow prediction on the PeMS dataset and electricity consumption on the M4 competition dataset).
CONTROLS: Compare against baseline models with no experience replay, models with fixed buffer size, and models with adaptive buffer size.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: We expect experience replay to improve the robustness of online forecasts when dealing with distribution shift, particularly whenSelector when the historical data remains relevant, although the effectiveness might degrade when concept drifts differ from the past.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Adapters on Pre-Trained Models for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop and compare a range of adapters (e.g., shallow networks, kernel-based methods, and self-attention mechanisms) for pre-trained deep forecasting models (e.g., Prophet, LSTM, and GRU) on both simulated and real-world datasets (e.g., traffic flow prediction on the PeMS dataset and electricity consumption on the M4 competition dataset).
CONTROLS: Compare against baseline models with no adapter and a standard frozen base model with adaptive layer.
COST: 3372
PREDICTION: We expect adapters to focusing on adapting certain aspects of the pre-trained model to handle concept drifts or distribution shifts, better than other methods of adapting weights of large models, but there might be challenges in balancing between adding too little capabilities to the pre-trained model and completely producing a new model.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Evaluating the Utilization of Historical Data through Experience Replay for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Modify the experience replay experiment to incorporate the use of a meta-model (e.g., Bayes' neural network or a neural network with learnable parameters as function of time) that balances the exploitation of online learning and the exploration of historical data across a range of real-world benchmarks (e.g., traffic flow prediction on the PeMS dataset and electricity consumption on the M4 competition dataset).
CONTROLS: Compare against baseline models with no experience replay, models with fixed buffer size, models with adaptive buffer size, and models using a standard experience replay strategy without a meta-model.
COST: 2680
PREDICTION: We expect the meta-model to adapt the replay strategy over time to improve the robustness of online forecasts and handle distribution shifts, particularly when the meta-model is able to effectively adapt to changes in the patterns present in the data.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Delays in Feedback and Gradient Estimation for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of delayed feedback and gradient estimation on the performance of online time series forecasting models (e.g., Prophet, LSTM, and GRU) on synthetic and real-world datasets (e.g., traffic flow prediction on the PeMS dataset and electricity consumption on the M4 competition dataset).
CONTROLS: Compare against baseline models with immediate feedback and gradient estimation, models with simulated delays, and models using gradient approximation techniques.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: We expect delayed feedback and gradient estimation to negatively impact the performance of online time series forecasting models, particularly on longer-term forecasts, but models leveraging techniques such as gradient approximation might mitigate these effects.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Autonomous Dynamic Regularization for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate a novel approach to dynamic regularization that adapts its strength over time based on the changing patterns in the data and the performance of the model (e.g., through monitoring the stability of the forecast or the magnitude of the gradients).
CONTROLS: Compare against baseline models with fixed regularization strength, models with traditional regularization (e.g., L1 and L2), and models using other forms of dynamic regularization.
COST: 4400
PREDICTION: We expect the autonomous dynamic regularization to improve the robustness and adaptability of online time series forecasting models by effectively balancing exploration and exploitation, but might face difficulties in balancing between over-regularization and under-regularization in certain situations.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Online Transfer Learning for Time Series Forecasting acrossRelatedDomains
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of online transfer learning to leverage knowledge from a related domain (e.g., traffic flow forecasting and electricity consumption forecasting) to improve the performance of a time series forecasting model in a target domain.
CONTROLS: Compare against baseline models trained from scratch in the target domain, models using offline transfer learning, and models using other forms of transfer learning (e.g., multi-task learning).
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: We expect online transfer learning to improve the performance of time series forecasting models, particularly in situations where the related domains share similar patterns and the target domain is in a state of concept drift, but might face challenges when the related domain and target domain are dissimilar or have diverging patterns.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: A Theoretical Analysis of Dynamic Regret in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework to analyze the dynamic regret of online time series forecasting algorithms, including bounds on the dynamic regret and conditions for optimality.
CONTROLS: Compare against existing theoretical results and analyze the implications for practical algorithm design.
COST: 5330 (compute hours are higher due to the complexity of theoretical proofs and analysis)
PREDICTION: We expect the theoretical framework to provide insights into the design of efficient online time series forecasting algorithms and the trade-offs between exploration and exploitation, but may face challenges in extending the analysis to non-stationary environments with abrupt concept drifts.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating the Efficacy of Frozen Base Models with Adaptive Layers for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Modify the experiment to incorporate a more comprehensive evaluation of the frozen base models with adaptive layers, including a comparison with state-of-the-art online time series forecasting methods and a detailed analysis of their performance on a range of real-world benchmarks (e.g., traffic flow prediction on the PeMS dataset, electricity consumption on the M4 competition dataset).
CONTROLS: Compare against baseline models with unfrozen base models and no adaptive layers, models using ensembling strategies, and models with other forms of adapters.
COST: 8400
PREDICTION: We expect the revised experiment to provide a more thorough understanding of the strengths and limitations of frozen base models with adaptive layers and their potential to improve the performance of online time series forecasting, but may face challenges in benchmarking against the latest state-of-the-art methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploration of Lightweight Dense Text Retrievers for Enhancing Vision-Centric Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: Experimentally evaluate the performance of ColPali-based encoders paired with a lightweight dense text retriever (e.g., Anaconda) on visual document retrieval benchmarks (e.g., MS MARCO, QCPR). Compare with the ColPali-based encoder alone, and ablate the dense text retriever to understand its contribution.
CONTROLS: ColPali-based encoder without dense text retriever, BM25 with image encoding, and a vector space model (VSM) with visual features.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The lightweight dense text retriever will improve ColPali-based encoder's performance on recall and precision metrics, and well-ablate to justify its contribution; however, it might fail to improve if the baseline ColPali-based encoder already has high performance on the benchmarks used.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Exploration of Lightweight Dense Text Retrievers for Enhancing Vision-Centric Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: Experimentally evaluate the performance of ColPali-based encoders paired with a lightweight dense text retriever (e.g., Anaconda) on visual document retrieval benchmarks (e.g., MS MARCO, QCPR). Include variants of the Anaconda retriever with TCT-ColBERT and ColBERT late-interaction as base models, and compare their performance. Compare with the ColPali-based encoder alone, and ablate the dense text retriever to understand its contribution.
CONTROLS: ColPali-based encoder without dense text retriever, BM25 with image encoding, and a vector space model (VSM) with visual features, as well as aggregating the scores of ColPali-based encoder and BM25.
COST: 4338.929
PREDICTION: The variants of Anaconda retriever with different base models will show varying levels of performance improvement over the ColPali-based encoder, and ablation will justify its contribution. However, performance gains might be limited if the baseline ColPali-based encoder already has high performance on the benchmarks used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing an Architecture-Agnostic Hybrid Retriver for Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Propose a new hybrid retriever architecture that aggregates the representations of a vision-centric multimodal encoder (e.g., ColPali) and a dense text retriever (e.g., Anaconda) directly at query time, using late interaction to combine their signals. Evaluate this architecture on visual document retrieval benchmarks (e.g., MS MARCO, QCPR) paired with ColPali and Anaconda from previous proposals, and compare with a baseline of summing their scores.
CONTROLS: Baseline of summing ColPali's and Anaconda's scores, individual ColPali and Anaconda models, BM25 with image encoding, and a vector space model (VSM) with visual features.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: The proposed hybrid retriever will improve retrieval quality over the individual models and baseline, especially for query-document pairs with complementary visual and textual signals, but may face challenges in effectively combining heterogeneous signals and may fail if the individual models are too strong or too weak.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Developing an Architecture-Agnostic Hybrid Retriver for Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Propose a new hybrid retriever architecture that aggregates the representations of a vision-centric multimodal encoder (e.g., ColPali) and a dense text retriever (e.g., Anaconda) directly at query time, using late interaction to combine their signals. To address heterogeneity, propose a normalizing technique that takes the maximum cosine similarity between all pairs of vectors from the two models, and devises an efficient online aggregation algorithm to accommodate strict latency and memory budgets. Evaluate this architecture on visual document retrieval benchmarks (e.g., MS MARCO, QCPR) paired with ColPali and Anaconda from previous proposals, and compare with a baseline of summing their scores.
CONTROLS: Baseline of summing ColPali's and Anaconda's scores, individual ColPali and Anaconda models, BM25 with image encoding, and a vector space model (VSM) with visual features, as well as a hybrid version without normalizing technique.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: The proposed hybrid retriever will improve retrieval quality over the individual models and baseline, and normalizing technique will effectively resolve heterogeneity issue; however, implementing online aggregation algorithm may lead to latency and overhead, and possibly fail if normalizing technique does not perform well on all scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Modal-Type Impact on Hybridization in Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Investigate how the modality type (textual, visual, or multimodal) affects the performance and heterogeneity of hybrid retrieval. Conduct experiments on visual document retrieval benchmarks (e.g., MS MARCO, QCPR) using different combinations of modal-type encoders (e.g., textual Anaconda, visual ColPali, multimodal ColPali) in the hybrid retriever, and analyze the effect of modal-type mismatch on hybrid retrieval performance.
CONTROLS: Baselines of individual modal-type encoders, architecture-agnostic hybrid retriever with normalizing technique and without normalizing technique, and statistical analysis of experiment results.
COST: 10680
PREDICTION: Different modality types will have varying impacts on hybrid retrieval performance, with multimodal representations generally performing best, but also most heterogeneous; however, this may depend on the specific benchmarks and datasets used, and possibly fail if the modal-type mismatch is too large.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Investigating the Modal-Type Impact on Hybridization in Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Investigate how the modality type (textual, visual, or multimodal) affects the performance and heterogeneity of hybrid retrieval. Specifically, evaluate the effect of using strong vs. weak textual and visual encoders in the hybrid retriever. Conduct experiments on visual document retrieval benchmarks (e.g., MS MARCO, QCPR) using different combinations of strong (e.g., ColBERT) and weak (e.g., BM25) textual and visual encoders in the hybrid retriever, and analyze the effect of modal-type mismatch on hybrid retrieval performance.
CONTROLS: Baselines of individual strong and weak modal-type encoders, architecture-agnostic hybrid retriever with normalizing technique and without normalizing technique, and statistical analysis of experiment results.
COST: 16000
PREDICTION: Using strong textual and visual encoders in the hybrid retriever will lead to best performance, but also most heterogeneity, while using weak encoders will reduce heterogeneity but compromise performance; however, this may depend on the specific benchmarks and datasets used, and possibly fail if the modal-type mismatch is too large.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Online Aggregation Overhead in Hybrid Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Investigate the online aggregation overhead of the proposed architecture-agnostic hybrid retriever in real-world scenarios. Utilize a production-level visual document retrieval system to benchmark the performance and latency overhead of the hybrid retriever with normalizing technique, compared to a baseline system using individual models. Conduct experiments on large-scale datasets (e.g., a million documents) and analyze the effect of different aggregation frequencies and chunk sizes on latency and performance.
CONTROLS: Baselines of individual ColPali and Anaconda models, architecture-agnostic hybrid retriever with normalizing technique and without normalizing technique, and production-level visual document retrieval system.
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: The online aggregation overhead will be minimal and the hybrid retriever will outperform individual models in terms of recall and precision, but may suffer from increased latency for high-frequency aggregation and large chunk sizes; however, this may depend on the specific hardware and software configurations used, and possibly fail if the aggregation overhead is too high.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Trade-off Between Retrieval Quality, Online Latency, and Index Memory in Hybrid Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Investigate the trade-off between retrieval quality, online latency, and index memory in the proposed hybrid retriever architecture. Conduct systematic experiments by varying model sizes, encoding complexities, and index compression techniques, and analyze the effects on retrieval quality, online latency, and index memory usage. Evaluate the hybrid retriever on large-scale datasets (e.g., a million documents) and compare its performance with baselines using individual models.
CONTROLS: Baselines of individual ColPali and Anaconda models, architecture-agnostic hybrid retriever with normalizing technique and without normalizing technique, and various index compression techniques.
COST: 28800
PREDICTION: The hybrid retriever will require significant trade-offs between retrieval quality, online latency, and index memory usage, but will generally outperform individual models in terms of recall and precision for medium to large model sizes and encoding complexities; however, this may depend on the specific hardware and software configurations used, and possibly fail if the trade-off is too extreme.

ACTION: ADD
